sections.html:
Fort Smith sits on the Oklahoma line in western Arkansas, where the Arkansas and Poteau rivers meet. Sebastian County has two seats, and this is one of them. Population was 89,142 in 2020 and is estimated at 90,855 for 2025, third among Arkansas cities. The metro area spills into Oklahoma, so buyers and employers come from both states.

The housing stock is mixed. Older neighborhoods downtown, including the 22-block Belle Grove Historic District, hold restored homes from many eras, while Chaffee Crossing in east Fort Smith is a newer zone on former military land. If your house is in a historic district, ask the city planning department what exterior work is allowed before you repair or replace anything for a sale.

Homes around the downtown historic sites date far back, and many still have their original wiring, plumbing and plaster. Write down what has been updated and when, and hold on to permits for any work. A dated list of upgrades answers an inspector's opening questions in advance.

Older houses also tend to need a closer look at the electrical panel and the plumbing lines. If you replaced either one, keep the permit and the contractor's invoice with your sale folder.

Health care, manufacturing, trucking and public education lead the job market, with Mercy-Fort Smith, Fort Smith Public Schools and ArcBest at the top of the employer list. When a plant changes shifts or a company moves a department, some owners have to sell faster than a normal listing allows. Transport and logistics work means many households depend on highways and freight.

After you accept an offer, the title company opens a file, checks the deed for every owner of record, and searches for liens. A tax balance or a city lien shows up in that search. The settlement statement then lists the payoff of any mortgage, the split of the current year's tax and the deed transfer tax. A flood or storm history can slow things down only if the paperwork is missing, which is why the insurance claims and repair invoices matter. A cash sale has no lender appraisal, so the schedule depends mostly on how fast the title work finishes. Sellers who bring their documents on the first day usually close sooner.

sections.h2: Flood risk along the Arkansas River
sections.html:
Fort Smith has real flood history. In May 2019 the Arkansas River hit record levels, and flow at Trimble Lock and Dam near the city climbed from 170,000 cubic feet per second on May 22 to more than 500,000 across the river soon afterward. About 545 homes in Sebastian County were affected, and floodwater also backed up into Massard Creek.

A house that took on water, or sits near the river, needs paperwork before it is sold. Pull together any insurance claim, repair invoices and permit records. Buyers will ask whether the property is in a mapped flood zone, and you can look up your address on the FEMA flood map service.

• Insurance claim letters and payout records.
  • Invoices for drying out, repairs and replaced materials.
  • Permits for any structural, electrical or plumbing work done afterward.
  • The FEMA flood map result for your address.

A seller with this folder ready can answer the first question every buyer asks, which is whether the house has taken on water. A seller without it usually gets a lower offer, because the buyer has to assume the worst. This holds for cash buyers and for lender-financed buyers alike, since a lender may require flood insurance in a mapped zone and will want to see the history.

July averages 83.1 degrees, and about 47.34 inches of precipitation fall in a typical year. Major tornadoes hit the city in 1898, 1927 and 1996, which is why buyers look hard at roofs.

  • Have a roofer check shingles and flashing after hail season.
  • Keep records of storm repairs and insurance payouts.
  • Confirm that the crawlspace drains and any sump pump work.

sections.h2: Schools, roads and the river port
sections.html: The Fort Smith School District operates 26 schools, including two high schools, four middle schools and 19 elementary schools, plus one alternative school. The University of Arkansas at Fort Smith is in town too. The city lies just southwest of where I-40 and I-49 meet, and US 64, US 71 and US 271 also serve it. Fort Smith Regional Airport has commercial service to Dallas/Fort Worth, and the Port of Fort Smith handles barge traffic on the Arkansas River.

TaskDeadline or window
Pay real estate taxMarch 1 through October 15
Assess personal propertyJanuary 1 through May 31
Correct assessment information or appeal to the Equalization BoardThird Monday in August
Apply for homestead credit on a primary residenceOctober 15

Once October 15 passes, real estate tax is delinquent and a 10% penalty applies. Personal property left unassessed after May 31 carries a separate 10% state penalty, and it cannot be waived. City liens must be paid before or with taxes, so a lien on your house can hold up a payment.

sections.h2: Tax relief for seniors and disabled owners
sections.html:
An owner who is 65 or older, or disabled, may request a value freeze on a principal residence. A home owner with a 100% service-connected disability rating must submit a VA letter by October 15 each year. Call the Sebastian County assessor's office to start either request.

Arkansas also taxes the deed itself at $3.30 per $1,000 of the sale price, so plan for it in your closing costs.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes or liens owed
sections.html: Owing tax or a city lien will not block a closing. Whatever is outstanding comes out of your proceeds, so hand the title company the exact amounts on day one. Call the county collector for the tax amount and the city for any lien payoff. Do this before you accept an offer so that the number you compare is what you would really keep.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale make sense in Fort Smith?
sections.html:
Cash buying tends to fit homes with flood history, roof or foundation work put off for years, a probate case, or a tenant living there. A conventional buyer's lender will order an appraisal and may require repairs, and a deal can fall apart on an older or damaged house. A cash buyer skips both steps.

Gather your deed, a mortgage payoff statement, any lien information and recent tax bills. With those in hand you can compare a cash offer, a listing and a sale by owner on cost and time, and the title company can move quickly once you pick one.

If the house is in a probate case, confirm early who has authority to sign. If a tenant lives there, tell the buyer about the lease before the first walk-through.

faqs.q: Is Fort Smith in a flood zone?
faqs.a: Parts of it are. The Arkansas River reached record levels in 2019, and about 545 homes in Sebastian County were affected. Check your address on the FEMA flood map service.

faqs.q: When are Sebastian County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Between March 1 and October 15. After October 15 the collector adds a 10% penalty.

faqs.q: When is the deadline to appeal an assessment in Sebastian County?
faqs.a: Corrections and Equalization Board appeals are due the third Monday in August each year.

faqs.q: What is the real property transfer tax in Arkansas?
faqs.a: It is $3.30 per $1,000 of the actual price on deeds that convey real estate, run by the state Department of Finance and Administration.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Fort Smith house that had flood damage?
faqs.a: Yes. Provide repair and insurance records if you have them. A cash buyer can take the house in its current condition.
